aboutMore: ok serious riley time (10 seconds) (rawr): i babysit the hendricks twins, milo and jade (5), on tuesdays and thursdays and i'm honestly the best babysitter in parma. red cross certificate on the fridge, taco shaped band-aids in my bag, zero failures. invisible cookies started when i was 8: the week before payday the grocery money ran low and my dad handed me an empty plate and said 'chocolate chip. premium.' i believed him. i've been handing them out ever since. my dad drives the 5 AM bread truck. he's the real random one, he just doesn't announce it. blog.title: BABYSITTING REPORT: milo and jade (5) (and me) (tuesday)
blog.body: every tuesday and thursday i babysit the hendricks twins down the street, milo and jade, they're 5. today they asked what animal i'd be and i said RACCOON and they SCREAMED and drew stripes on their faces with markers (washable, i checked, i ALWAYS check) and now there are 3 raccoons in the living room. jade fell off the couch and started crying and i handed her an invisible cookie and said 'it's chocolate chip, premium' and she took a bite and said 'it's good' and stopped crying. that's the whole trick. i have a red cross certificate and a taco band-aid and zero failures. mrs hendricks pays me $9 an hour plus a real cookie (a REAL one, it feels weird, i save half for the invisible ones, it's a lot of math). when i grow up i want to do 2 things: babysit and be GIR.

blog.title: where invisible cookies come from (a serious one)
blog.body: ok people always ask. here's the true story. i was 8. it was the week before payday. there were no cookies and no money and my mom was working a double. my dad came into the kitchen after his 5 AM route (he drives the bread truck) and handed me an empty plate and said 'chocolate chip. premium.' i looked at the plate. i looked at him. he looked kind of nervous. and i just... took one. i ate it. i said 'dad this is the best one yet.' he laughed so hard he had to sit on the kitchen floor. that's the whole story. every invisible cookie i've ever given out is from that night. they never go stale. they're always fresh. they're the best thing i've ever eaten. rawr. (that means thank you in dinosaur.) (it also means i love you.) (it means both.)

blog.title: I MET A REAL RACCOON (a transcript)
blog.body: it was 11:40 PM. i took the trash out. there was a RACCOON on the can. a real one. with stripes. a REAL ONE. we looked at each other for 4 minutes. i said 'rawr.' he did nothing. i said 'rawr' again but sweeter. he held a chicken bone in both hands like a tiny person at a banquet. i said 'i do my stripes with eyeliner and it takes 20 minutes.' he blinked. i said 'you're better at it.' he left. i went inside and said 'dad. dad. i've been SEEN.' my dad said 'riley it's midnight.' i said 'DAD HE WAS A RACCOON.' he said 'good for him.' i've named him Gir Junior. my mom says he's the reason the can is always open. i don't care. he's the best thing that's happened to me this week. (the first was milo's stripes.)

blog.title: what's in my bag (a tour) (it's a lot)
blog.body: 1) travel hairspray (Little Destiny). 2) a fold up straightener (Destiny's cousin, she's anxious). 3) taco band-aids (3) for babysitting emergencies. 4) 4 safety pins (a dress emergency once, nobody knows). 5) 7 glow bracelets. 6) a mood ring that's been green since august (it's broken but i like green). 7) one invisible cookie, always in reserve. 8) a note from my dad: 'proud of you. don't forget your lunch.' (i forgot my lunch.) 9) a spare GIR sticker. 10) a gas station gift card with $3 on it from mr darnell, because i did my first stripes in his bathroom and he said 'you're my favorite customer, you only ever ask for the key.' it's a small thing. it's in the bag. all of it matters.
